title: The Wide World
subtitle: What's out there to find, by land and by sea.

quests.title: Redwood Giants
description: Biomes O' Plenty adds dozens of new biomes. Start with a Redwood Forest, where redwood trees grow tall on thick trunks.
Keep your eyes open as you travel: this chapter only names a few.

quests.title: Lavender Fields
description: Lavender Fields are open meadows grown over with lavender, easy ground to travel.
A map helps you find your way back to the ones you like.

quests.title: The Glowing Grotto
description: Underground, the Glowing Grotto is a cave lit by glowshrooms, glowing moss and hanging strands of glowworm silk.
Look for it while you mine, and bring torches for the dark stretches on the way.

quests.title: Crystalline Chasm
description: In the Nether, Biomes O' Plenty's Crystalline Chasm is grown through with rose quartz.
About a third of this Nether is Biomes O' Plenty's; the rest is vanilla's, so it can take some searching.

quests.title: The Ice Maze
description: Aquamirae's Ice Maze spreads over the Deep Frozen Ocean: a maze of ice with frozen pirate ships and outposts in it, and creatures that hunt in the cold water.
Bring a boat, food and light. Its bosses have their own chapter.

quests.title: Left Behind
description: The Ice Maze's pirates left Pirate Pouches behind them. Search the maze for one and see what they couldn't carry.

quests.title: Disturbing the Dead
description: The Graveyard fills the world with burial grounds: small graves in many places, graveyards in forests, larger ones in taigas and sandy ones in deserts.
Step into a forest graveyard. The dead there don't rest easy, so come armed.

quests.title: Too Late
description: Some villages were overrun before you got there: charred houses and tormented villagers. They turn up in plains, deserts, savannas, taigas and snowy clearings.
Tormented villagers can be redeemed with a bell.

quests.title: The Harvest Court
description: Born in Chaos's pumpkin folk walk the open land at night, all year, though you'll rarely meet them: Mr. and Mrs. Pumpkin, Senor Pumpkin and Pumpkin Bruisers. Their knight, Sir Pumpkinhead, roams on horseback (Summoned & Roaming, in the boss chapters).
They keep to the surface under the night sky, not caves. The mod's other creatures turn up as sentinels and around its graves and towers.

quests.title: Sentinels
description: By day, about once a day, a lone sentinel may stand guard somewhere near you: knights and haunted armor on open land, lumberjacks, wood golems and the Spiders Mother in woods, frost giants and the Amarok in snow, now and then a bone dinosaur in the desert.

A sentinel holds its spot and only comes for you within 16 blocks, so you choose the fight. Dreadknights can stand anywhere, and so, rarely, can a Mutant Enderman: leave him be and don't stare. Now and then a pillager scout wanders by instead.

quests.title: War Bands
description: From day 5, illager war bands march by day the way patrols do, away from villages: pillagers, vindicators and Illager Invasion's marauders, provokers, alchemists and the odd basher.
The one carrying the banner leads. Kill it and you get Bad Omen, as with a patrol.

quests.title: Pirates Ashore
description: From day 3, pirate bands land on beaches and shores by the sea near you, day or night: Bosses'Rise's rooks and crossbow pirates, led by a rook, and quicker than the Kraken's crew.
A band pirate you've hit may drop a Pirate Chart when it dies.

quests.title: Pirate Charts
description: Pirate Charts come from band pirates you've hit (about one in fifteen), from buried treasure (more often than not) and from shipwreck chests.
Use one in the Overworld to read it: it becomes a treasure map to the lair of a boss no one on this world has beaten yet, within about 3000 blocks. It crumbles when you reach the X.
It's the surest way to find the bosses in the Bosses chapters.
